\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{कैवणो} (kaivṇo)}{कैवणो (kaivṇo)}]{\mw{कैवणो} (kaivṇo) — to say}

\label{lesson:MW-C268-kaivno}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for waiting, then the Marwadi for to hold on.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{कैवणो}}
\textbf{\mw{कैवणो}} — \emph{kaivṇo} — \textquotedblleft{}to say\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{वो} \mw{साची} \mw{बात} \mw{कैवै} \mw{है।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{vo sāchī bāt kaivai hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He tells the truth.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \mw{म्हैं} \mw{एक} \mw{सबद} \mw{कोनी} \mw{कैयो}, \emph{mhaĩ ek sabad konī kaiyo}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{कैवणो}} (\emph{kaivṇo}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{kathayati}, \textquotedblleft{}converses with, describes\textquotedblright{}; CDIAL lists the Old Marwari forms \emph{kahaï} and \emph{kai} under it (CDIAL 2703).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for asking and answering.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kaivṇo}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kaivṇo}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vo sāchī bāt kaivai hai.} — He tells the truth.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marwadi for waiting, then the Marwadi for to hold on, then say \emph{kaivṇo} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \mw{कैवणो} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To say\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{सुणावणो} (suṇāvṇo)}{सुणावणो (suṇāvṇo)}]{\mw{सुणावणो} (suṇāvṇo) — to recite; to tell (a story)}

\label{lesson:MW-C268-sunavno}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for to hold on, then the Marwadi for to say.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{सुणावणो}}
\textbf{\mw{सुणावणो}} — \emph{suṇāvṇo} — \textquotedblleft{}to recite; to tell (a story)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{दादी} \mw{गीत} \mw{सुणावै} \mw{है।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dādī gīt suṇāvai hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Grandmother recites a song.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \mw{म्हैं} \mw{गीत} \mw{सुणायो}, \emph{mhaĩ gīt suṇāyo}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{सुणावणो}} (\emph{suṇāvṇo}) is built on \textbf{\mw{सुणणो}}, to hear, as its causative: \textquotedblleft{}to make someone hear\textquotedblright{}. CDIAL lists Marwari \emph{suṇṇo}, \textquotedblleft{}hears\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{śṛṇoti} (CDIAL 12598).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for asking and answering.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{सलाह} (salāh)}{सलाह (salāh)}]{\mw{सलाह} (salāh) — counsel; advice}

\label{lesson:MW-C268-salah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for to say, then the Marwadi for to recite.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{सलाह}}
\textbf{\mw{सलाह}} — \emph{salāh} — \textquotedblleft{}counsel; advice\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{दादी} \mw{चोखी} \mw{सलाह} \mw{देवै} \mw{है।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dādī chokhī salāh devai hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Grandmother gives good advice.
\end{quote}

A feminine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{सलाह}} (\emph{salāh}) is usually traced, through Persian \emph{salāh}, to Arabic \emph{ṣalāḥ}, \textquotedblleft{}counsel\textquotedblright{}. It is feminine: \textbf{\mw{चोखी} \mw{सलाह}}, good advice.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for asking and answering.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marwadi for to say, then the Marwadi for to recite, then say \emph{salāh} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{मतलब} (matlab)}{मतलब (matlab)}]{\mw{मतलब} (matlab) — a meaning; what someone means}

\label{lesson:MW-C268-matlab}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for to recite, then the Marwadi for counsel.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{मतलब}}
\textbf{\mw{मतलब}} — \emph{matlab} — \textquotedblleft{}a meaning; what someone means\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{थारो} \mw{मतलब} \mw{कांई} \mw{है}?
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{thāro matlab kāĩ hai?}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
What do you mean?
\end{quote}

A masculine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{मतलब}} (\emph{matlab}) is usually traced, through Persian \emph{matlab}, to Arabic \emph{maṭlab}, \textquotedblleft{}something sought, an aim\textquotedblright{}; the sense \textquotedblleft{}what someone means\textquotedblright{} is the one the word has in everyday use. It is masculine: \textbf{\mw{थारो} \mw{मतलब}}, what you mean.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for asking and answering.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marwadi for to recite, then the Marwadi for counsel, then say \emph{matlab} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{सिफारस} (siphāras)}{सिफारस (siphāras)}]{\mw{सिफारस} (siphāras) — a good word for someone; a recommendation}

\label{lesson:MW-C268-sipharas}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for counsel, then the Marwadi for a meaning.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{सिफारस}}
\textbf{\mw{सिफारस}} — \emph{siphāras} — \textquotedblleft{}a good word for someone; a recommendation\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{भाई} \mw{म्हारी} \mw{सिफारस} \mw{करै} \mw{है।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bhāī mhārī siphāras karai hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My brother puts in a good word for me.
\end{quote}

A feminine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{सिफारस}} (\emph{siphāras}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{sifārish}, \textquotedblleft{}a recommendation\textquotedblright{}. It is feminine: \textbf{\mw{म्हारी} \mw{सिफारस}}, a good word for me.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for asking and answering.
